question.problem:
Suppose that $|\,p\,|=6$, $|\,q\,|=12$ and that the angle between the vectors is $\theta ={150}^{∘}.$ Find the vector projection of $q$ onto $p$ in terms of the vector $p.$

${\text{proj}}_{p}\,q=$
{{field-1}}
$p$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the scalar projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{p}\,q & =|\,q\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =12\operatorname{cos}⁡({150}^{∘}) \\  & =12\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-6\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the unit vector that is parallel to $p:$

$$
u=\frac{p}{|\,p\,|}=\frac{p}{6}=\frac{1}{6}p
$$

Finally, we compute the vector projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{p}\,q & ={\text{comp}}_{p}\,q\cdot u \\  & =-6\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac{1}{6}p \\  & =-\sqrt{3}\,p\end{aligned}
$$
